pageInfo.subtitle: Master the expressive techniques that bring emotion and personality to your playing through controlled pitch manipulation and musical vibrato.
pageInfo.heroDescription: Bending and vibrato are the most expressive techniques in guitar playing, allowing you to add emotion, personality, and vocal-like qualities to your music. These techniques transform static notes into living, breathing musical expressions that can convey everything from subtle sophistication to raw emotional power. Mastering these skills is essential for blues, rock, jazz, and virtually every guitar style.

items.text: Use multiple fingers for strength and control
Push or pull strings perpendicular to fretboard
Practice smooth bend and release motions
Control speed and width of oscillation
Use wrist and finger motion coordination
Match vibrato style to musical context

exercises.title: Half-Step Bends
exercises.description: Start with subtle half-step (semitone) bends to develop control and pitch accuracy. These small bends are essential for blues, jazz, and expressive playing.

patternNote.text: Target: Bend up exactly one fret's worth of pitch

practiceNotes.title: Practice Notes
practiceNotes.text: Use your ring finger supported by middle and index fingers. Bend slowly and listen carefully to match the target pitch. Practice on different strings to feel the varying resistance.

exercises.title: Whole-Step Bends
exercises.description: Master the classic whole-step (whole tone) bend - the most common and recognizable bend in blues and rock guitar. This is the foundation of expressive lead playing.

patternNote.text: Target: Bend up exactly two frets' worth of pitch

practiceNotes.title: Practice Notes
practiceNotes.text: Use all three fingers behind the bending finger for maximum strength. This bend should sound exactly like the note two frets higher. Practice bending up and releasing slowly.
practiceNotes.tempo: The most important bend to master

exercises.title: Pre-Bends and Releases
exercises.description: Learn to bend strings before picking (pre-bend) and then release them for a descending pitch effect. This creates unique tonal colors and emotional expression.

patternNote.text: Technique: Silent bend up, pick, then release down

notation.title: Pre-Bends with Releases: Descending Pitch Effects

practiceNotes.title: Practice Notes
practiceNotes.text: Bend the string silently to target pitch first, then pick and slowly release. The goal is a smooth descending pitch without any attack on the bent note.

exercises.title: Multiple String Bends
exercises.description: Bend multiple strings simultaneously or in sequence to create harmonized bends and complex pitch relationships that add richness to your melodic lines.

patternNote.text: Challenge: Controlling multiple strings with different bend amounts

practiceNotes.title: Practice Notes
practiceNotes.text: Use one finger per string and coordinate the bending motion. Start with unison bends (same pitch on different strings) before attempting harmony bends.

exercises.title: Bend and Hold with Vibrato
exercises.description: Combine bending with vibrato to create the most expressive technique in guitar playing. This is essential for blues, rock solos, and emotional musical expression.

patternNote.text: Technique: Bend to pitch, hold, then apply vibrato

practiceNotes.title: Practice Notes
practiceNotes.text: Bend to the target pitch and hold it steady, then apply gentle vibrato. The vibrato should be controlled and musical, not wild or erratic.
practiceNotes.tempo: The signature sound of expressive guitar

exercises.title: Basic Vibrato Control
exercises.description: Develop consistent, controlled vibrato that adds life and emotion to sustained notes. Master different speeds and widths to match various musical contexts.

patternNote.text: Focus: Consistent oscillation speed and pitch width

notation.title: Sustained Notes with Vibrato on Different Strings

practiceNotes.title: Practice Notes
practiceNotes.text: Start the vibrato motion after the note is clearly established. Use wrist motion primarily, with finger support. Practice both fast and slow vibrato speeds.

exercises.title: Delayed Vibrato Entry
exercises.description: Master the sophisticated technique of delayed vibrato - letting the note ring clearly before gradually introducing vibrato for maximum emotional impact.

patternNote.text: Timing: Note -> Silence -> Gradual vibrato introduction

practiceNotes.title: Practice Notes
practiceNotes.text: Let the initial note ring cleanly, then gradually introduce vibrato. This creates dramatic tension and is very effective for climactic moments in solos.

exercises.title: Vibrato Width Control
exercises.description: Learn to control the width (pitch deviation) of your vibrato to match different musical styles - from subtle jazz vibrato to wide blues/rock expression.

notation.title: Vibrato on Different Strings and Positions

practiceNotes.title: Practice Notes
practiceNotes.text: Practice the same note with different vibrato widths. Narrow vibrato for jazz/classical, medium for rock, wide for blues. Match the style to the musical context.

items.title: Technical Development
items: Start with reference notes to train pitch accuracy
Practice bends on all strings to feel resistance differences
Use multiple fingers for strength and control
Record yourself to evaluate pitch accuracy
Practice slow, controlled vibrato before attempting fast

challenges.title: Inaccurate Pitch
challenges.text: Practice with a tuner or backing track to verify target pitches. Play the target note first, then bend to match it.

challenges.title: Inconsistent Vibrato
challenges.text: Focus on regular, controlled motion. Practice with a metronome to develop consistent timing and rhythm.

challenges.title: Weak Finger Strength
challenges.text: Build up gradually with easier bends. Use multiple fingers for support and practice finger strengthening exercises.

items.reason: Light gauge strings (10-46) are easier to bend accurately without excess finger strain
Strat-style guitars with curved fretboard radius make string bending feel natural and comfortable
